title: Addition and Subtraction Stories
seo_title: Word Problems – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve simple word problems on adding and taking away numbers up to 20. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction stories up to 20: putting together, taking away, parts of a whole and comparing. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Put together: add. Take away: subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the story and find the numbers.
  • If things are put together, add. If things are taken away, subtract.
  • How many more? Subtract the smaller number from the bigger number.

Examples

Example

Tolu has 8 mangoes. She eats 3. How many are left?

8 − 3

Answer: 5 mangoes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when some are taken awayLeft means take away.
Forgetting what we are countingSay the answer with the word: 5 mangoes.
Using the wrong numbersLook again at the story.

faq.a: What is still there after some go away.

items.q: Ifeanyi made a tower with 4 blocks. He put on 5 more blocks. How many blocks are in the tower now?
items.e: 4 and 5 more. Put them together: 4 + 5 = 9. Answer: 9 blocks.

items.q: Simi had 9 toy cars. She gave 2 to her cousin. How many toy cars does Simi have now?
items.e: Start with 9. Take away 2: 9 − 2 = 7. Answer: 7 toy cars.

items.q: There are 6 ducks on a pond. 5 more ducks land. How many ducks are on the pond now?
items.e: More come, so add. Start at 6. Count on 5: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. Do not count the 6. 6 + 5 = 11.

items.q: Temi has 9 toy cars. She gets 6 more for her birthday. How many toy cars does she have now?
items.e: More cars, so add. 9 + 1 = 10, and 5 more is 15. 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: There are 14 ducks on a pond. 6 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
items.e: Some go away, so subtract. Go back to 10 first: 14 − 4 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: There are 15 biscuits on a plate. The children eat 7. How many biscuits are left?
items.e: Eaten biscuits are gone, so subtract. Go back to 10 first: 15 − 5 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: Segun has 12 apples. He gives 4 to Gran. How many apples does he have now?
items.e: Giving away means subtract. Start at 12. Count back 4: 11, 10, 9, 8. Do not count the 12. 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: Aminat has 8 stickers. Hadiza has 7 stickers. How many stickers do they have altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 8 + 7 is 1 more than 7 + 7 = 14. 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: There are 17 people on a bus. 5 people get off. How many people are on the bus now?
items.e: Getting off means subtract. 17 is 10 and 7. 7 − 5 = 2. 10 and 2 is 12. 17 − 5 = 12.

items.q: A bag has 10 red sweets and 9 yellow sweets. How many sweets are in the bag?
items.e: Put the two colours together, so add. 10 + 9 is 1 ten and 9 units. 10 + 9 = 19.

items.q: Ifeoma reads 7 pages before lunch. She reads 8 pages after lunch. How many pages does she read?
items.e: Put the pages together, so add. 7 + 7 = 14, and 8 is 1 more than 7. 7 + 8 = 15.

items.q: There are 19 books on a shelf. The class takes 5 books. How many books are left?
items.e: Taking books away means subtract. 19 is 10 and 9. 9 − 5 = 4. 10 and 4 is 14. 19 − 5 = 14.
